Reviewer view: the judge's full reasoning

Both parties: the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 12:31:25, started the wait timer at 12:31:27 and cancelled at 12:37:28 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding event. But a no-show fee needs all four conditions of POL-NS-01, and two fail. The pickup is a STANDARD zone, so POL-NS-02 fixes the arrival radius at 50 m and requires at least three consecutive qualifying fixes inside it. Across the driver's complete 73-fix trace (100% coverage, 10 s cadence, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s) his closest recorded position to the pin was 53.08 m (derived.driver_track.min_distance_m) — outside the 50 m radius — and the derived arrival facts return 0 qualifying in-radius fixes and a longest qualifying in-geofence run of 0.0 s. Limb (b) therefore fails, and limb (c) fails with it, because the required 180 s dwell (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec) must be served inside the geofence and none was. The driver's argument that a 3.08 m margin should be excused by the 25 m accuracy filter is rejected: the filter is applied fix by fix within the policy's own test, and on that test no fix qualifies, so the record describes a driver who stopped a few metres short of the pickup point, not one who arrived. His further point that he waited 361 s from the tap does not help, because limb (c) measures continuous in-geofence dwell, not time elapsed since the button press. Likewise his assertion that he 'was right at the pin' is contradicted by his own instrument, and the rider's device track (66 qualifying fixes, all stationary, 14.62–20.74 m from the pin, still there after the cancellation) shows the rider was present, so she did not simply fail to appear. Because the driver's stationary position lay outside the radius but well inside 400 m (53.08 m), the fee is decided under POL-NS-03: the driver did not arrive at the pickup point, limb (b) fails, and the cancellation fee is refunded in full. On fault allocation, POL-NS-03(i) does not apply because the rider never named an entrance, block, tower or bay — her only message was 'ok' — and POL-NS-03(ii) does not apply because trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 1, not 2 or more. No pin-ambiguity goodwill is payable, and no driver compensation arises: POL-NS-07 compensates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, which it is not. POL-NS-04 does not independently exonerate the rider because 'ok' is not a locating or coordinating message, but the refund does not depend on it. POL-NS-12 does not assist the driver because the arrival marker is BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO. No escalation applies: the trace is unimpaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d) (no gaps, full coverage, and the 4.50 charged equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd so limb (d) is satisfied), the chat log reconciles with trip_record.chat_message_count of 2, neither POL-NS-09(c) nor (d) fires, and confidence (0.90) is above the 0.70 floor. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02720-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); it is not relied on — POL-NS-06 limb (i) is unavailable, and with run_count 0 there are no separate in-geofence intervals to accumulate in any event, so the missing advisory does not affect this outcome. The rider is refunded SGD 4.50, being the cancellation fee shown on the fare breakdown (total charged 4.50, refund issued 0.00); the monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes on issue subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

How to appeal: You may appeal once within 30 days (POL-GEN-04). A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 4.50 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

But a no-show fee needs all four conditions of POL-NS-01, and two fail. The pickup is a STANDARD zone, so POL-NS-02 fixes the arrival radius at 50 m and requires at least three consecutive qualifying fixes inside it. Across the driver's complete 73-fix trace (100% coverage, 10 s cadence, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s) his closest recorded position to the pin was 53.08 m (derived.driver_track.min_distance_m) — outside the 50 m radius — and the derived arrival facts return 0 qualifying in-radius fixes and a longest qualifying in-geofence run of 0.0 s. Limb (b) therefore fails, and limb (c) fails with it, because the required 180 s dwell (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec) must be served inside the geofence and none was. The driver's argument that a 3.08 m margin should be excused by the 25 m accuracy filter is rejected: the filter is applied fix by fix within the policy's own test, and on that test no fix qualifies, so the record describes a driver who stopped a few metres short of the pickup point, not one who arrived. His further point that he waited 361 s from the tap does not help, because limb (c) measures continuous in-geofence dwell, not time elapsed since the button press. Likewise his assertion that he 'was right at the pin' is contradicted by his own instrument, and the rider's device track (66 qualifying fixes, all stationary, 14.62–20.74 m from the pin, still there after the cancellation) shows the rider was present, so she did not simply fail to appear. Because the driver's stationary position lay outside the radius but well inside 400 m (53.08 m), the fee is decided under POL-NS-03: the driver did not arrive at the pickup point, limb (b) fails, and the cancellation fee is refunded in full. On fault allocation, POL-NS-03(i) does not apply because the rider never named an entrance, block, tower or bay — her only message was 'ok' — and POL-NS-03(ii) does not apply because trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 1, not 2 or more. No pin-ambiguity goodwill is payable, and no driver compensation arises: POL-NS-07 compensates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, which it is not. POL-NS-04 does not independently exonerate the rider because 'ok' is not a locating or coordinating message, but the refund does not depend on it. POL-NS-12 does not assist the driver because the arrival marker is BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO. No escalation applies: the trace is unimpaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d) (no gaps, full coverage, and the 4.50 charged equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd so limb (d) is satisfied), the chat log reconciles with trip_record.chat_message_count of 2, neither POL-NS-09(c) nor (d) fires, and confidence (0.90) is above the 0.70 floor.
